definition.name: The Reluctant One — identity as a wager that becomes self-fulfilling
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Identity — Who am I, really? — and whether a self is discovered through destiny or forged through choice.
definition.summary: A man named 'the One' by a disembodied voice (ev-008) and offered a clean-slate identity by Smith (ev-007) spends the story rejecting the label, even denying he is the One as he commits to a rescue with no prophetic guarantee (ev-032). Each refusal is answered by behaviour that outruns his self-concept — leaping after Morpheus, halting bullets, reading the room as code (ev-034, ev-045) — until death and revival force him to seize the name he kept disowning (ev-045). The causal chain resolves the dilemma not by prophecy but by action: he becomes the One only after choosing to act as him, so identity is shown to be self-authored rather than pre-scripted (ev-039, ev-045).

chain.why_in_plot: A disembodied voice names Neo 'the One' and demands a 'Yes,' which is the exact offer of a clean-slate identity the plot is built around; Neo's refusal here seeds the rejection pattern the throughline tracks.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the chain's first entry: it is set moving by the Agents' interrogation and implantation (ev-007), whose planted tracker forces the crew to reclaim Neo and, in doing so, delivers him to the voice that first assigns him the name he will spend the story disowning.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong dread as destiny and offers a knowing/forgetting choice; Neo's swallowing the red pill is his first step into the identity the plot interrogates, even before he accepts the 'One' label.
chain.caused_by_previous: The bug's removal (ev-009) frees Neo's body from the tracker, enabling him to be brought to room 1313 and handed to Morpheus, whose destiny-framing directly continues the 'who am I' pressure the naming voice began.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus explicitly recasts the rescue as destiny via the myth of the One and declares 'the search is over,' cementing the pre-scripted identity that Neo will resist and that the plot's dilemma (destiny vs. choice) is defined against.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's waking and rebuilding (ev-012) and the 'desert of the real' revelation (ev-013) strip his old self-concept, leaving him 'recovered but spent' and therefore the receptive audience Morpheus addresses with the prophecy.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo commits to rescuing Morpheus while explicitly denying he is the One, so his mission becomes a wager on a man rather than a prophecy — the precise 'identity as a wager' mechanism the plot names (ev-032).
chain.caused_by_previous: Morpheus's capture and drugging into near-break (ev-031) creates the emergency that interrupts the crew's wake and forces Neo's choice; without Morpheus about to crack, there is no rescue to wager on.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo's behaviour outruns his self-concept: he guns down Agents, dives after the shot Morpheus, and catches him mid-fall — action that exceeds the 'not the One' identity he asserted in ev-032, exactly the 'each refusal answered by behaviour' pattern.
chain.caused_by_previous: The decision to go back in and Trinity's arming/command (ev-032) loads the crew's abilities and launches the helicopter assault; the rescue Neo committed to is the vehicle through which his ability now exceeds his self-belief.

chain.why_in_plot: Left alone with Smith, Neo chooses not to run and hardens into a gunfighter's calm — a choice to stand that Morpheus reads as 'the beginning of belief,' advancing the self-authored-identity arc between the rescue and the final confrontation.
chain.caused_by_previous: Trinity being ripped back to the ship and Tank refusing to send her back (ev-037) leaves Neo isolated in the subway with Smith trained on him, which is precisely the situation that forces his decision to turn and face the hunter.

chain.why_in_plot: At the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, summons an impossible surge, and hurls Smith into the ceiling — the clearest instance of power that outruns his self-concept, driven by the rejection itself.
chain.caused_by_previous: The bare-handed battle in which Smith chokes Neo near the electrified rail and frames his death as settled (ev-038→ev-039) pushes Neo to the brink where refusing the pronouned fate becomes the trigger for the surge.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo is killed by Smith and revived by Trinity's refusal to accept the ending — the death-and-revival crucible the plot identifies as what forces him to finally seize the name he kept disowning (ev-045 follows).
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's flight to the phone ending in Smith's point-blank shot (ev-043) is what kills him; the fatal shot is the direct consequence of the chase that the subway surge (ev-039) and subsequent flight (ev-041) set in motion.

chain.why_in_plot: Revived, Neo halts the Agents' volley, reads the room as flowing code, and destroys Smith from within — the moment he seizes the 'One' identity through action, resolving the dilemma by self-authorship rather than prophecy (ev-039, ev-045).
chain.caused_by_previous: Trinity's kiss restarting his heart (ev-044) is the revival that returns him with abilities that outrun any prior self-concept; the resurrection is the immediate cause of the halting of bullets and the code-vision that confirm him as the One.

definition.name: The Rescue — self-sacrifice as the price of becoming
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
definition.summary: Morpheus models the sacrifice horn by giving his life so Neo can escape (ev-025), and is then captured and tortured, setting up a debt Neo can only repay by going back into a world that will kill him (ev-031). Neo answers that precedent by stopping Morpheus's plug from being pulled and committing to a rescue he cannot justify by logic, only by faith (ev-032), then executes it against overwhelming force — dropping a helicopter, gunning down Agents, and catching Morpheus mid-fall (ev-034). The chain proves the dilemma's cost is real and reciprocal: the man Neo saves is the same man who died for him, so sacrifice is framed as the generative act that forges both identity and loyalty (ev-025, ev-032, ev-034).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the founding act of the plot: Morpheus 'choosing to give his own life so the others can escape' is the self-sacrifice that the throughline names as the price of becoming, and it creates the debt Neo must later repay.
chain.caused_by_previous: This is the first link; it sets the chain moving. The firefight in the wall (ev-024's escape into the plumbing) funnels the Agents onto the crew, so when 'an Agent ambushes Neo in the crawlspace,' Morpheus 'bursts through... and orders Trinity to get Neo out,' enacting the sacrifice.

chain.why_in_plot: It carries the direct consequence of ev-025: Morpheus stays behind to hold the Agents (he 'starts dominant strangling Agent Smith') and is taken, converting his self-sacrifice into an actual capture that the rescue must answer.
chain.caused_by_previous: Because Morpheus gave himself so the others could escape (ev-025), he is the one left 'upstairs in Room 808' fighting Smith while the survivors flee, which ends in his capture.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the torture that makes the debt urgent and concrete — Morpheus is being broken ('about to break,' 'fighting to keep his mind from cracking'), which is exactly the 'captured and tortured' state the summary says Neo must repay.
chain.caused_by_previous: The capture at the end of ev-026 delivers Morpheus into the Agents' hands, so here 'Agent Smith is already holding Morpheus captive' and escalates the interrogation toward breaking him.

chain.why_in_plot: This is Neo's answering move and the plot's pivot: he 'stops the plug from being pulled on Morpheus and commits to going back... to bring him out alive,' repaying the sacrifice 'not by logic, only by faith,' exactly as the theme frames it.
chain.caused_by_previous: Seeing Morpheus on the verge of breaking (ev-031) is what forces Neo to interrupt the wake and 'stop the plug from being pulled,' converting the torture into a rescue he cannot justify except by belief.

chain.why_in_plot: It is the execution of the rescue and the proof of the reciprocal cost: 'the man Neo saves is the same man who died for him,' so the generative sacrifice is completed and loyalty/identity are forged.
chain.caused_by_previous: Because Neo committed to the rescue in ev-032, he now 'drops the helicopter onto the executive office and guns down Agents,' extracts the 'unresponsive' Morpheus by force, and 'catches his handcuffed wrist before he hits the ground,' completing the chain Morpheus began in ev-025.

definition.name: The Betrayal — disillusionment choosing comfort over meaning
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Truth vs. a comfortable lie, and Meaning vs. pleasure — the counter-plot that tests the crew's cause from within.
definition.summary: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' (ev-020) and, savouring an impossible steak, bargains to be re-plugged into the lie, embodying the self-preservation and comfort horns the central plot refuses (ev-020). His resentment curdles into open treachery: he murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and stands over the comatose Neo — only to be struck down by Tank, who survived (ev-029). This causal chain is the story's negative proof: the same crisis that drives Neo toward meaning and sacrifice drives Cypher toward betrayal and death, so the crew's survival is purchased by purging the member who chose the comfortable lie (ev-020, ev-029).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's seed: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' and, savouring an impossible steak, bargains to be re-plugged into the lie — the comfort-over-meaning choice the plot is named for.
chain.caused_by_previous: First link in the chain; it sets the chain moving. Cypher's disillusionment and his deal with Smith establish the treachery every later act executes.

chain.why_in_plot: It shows Cypher operationalising his deal: while the crew moves toward the Oracle he covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can — the physical plant of the betrayal he bargained for in ev-020.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by ev-020's bargain: having agreed to deliver the crew, Cypher now plants the traceable phone that lets the Agents spring the trap.

chain.why_in_plot: The trap Cypher set closes: the Matrix is rewritten around the crew, Mouse is killed, and the group is sealed in — the 'body count' Cypher recast the prophecy as beginning to accrue.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by ev-021's planted phone: the dropped line is what lets the Agents rewrite the Matrix and spring the ambush on the crew.

chain.why_in_plot: It is a direct fruit of the betrayal's crisis: Morpheus chooses to give his life so Neo can escape, producing the captive Morpheus Cypher promised to deliver.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by ev-023's sealed trap: with the crew cornered, Morpheus seizes the traceable phone and then sacrifices himself, setting up his capture.

chain.why_in_plot: It completes the betrayal's first delivery: Morpheus is captured (the prize Cypher bargained to hand over), and Cypher's own disappearance begins, foreshadowing his turn on the ship.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by ev-025's sacrifice: Morpheus staying behind so others escape leads directly to his being taken, the commodity of Cypher's deal.

chain.why_in_plot: It positions Cypher, having reached the exit first, to strike: he climbs through to the ship and draws a concealed rifle — the setup for the open murder that follows.
chain.caused_by_previous: Enabled by ev-026's capture and the crew's flight: with Morpheus taken and the survivors routing to the exit, Cypher reaches the ship ahead of the others, weapon ready.

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's climax: Cypher's resentment curdles into open treachery — he murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and stands over comatose Neo — fulfilling the self-preservation/comfort horns the central plot refuses.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by ev-028's armed arrival: the concealed rifle Cypher draws on waking is the instrument he now uses to shoot Tank and murder the crew.

chain.why_in_plot: It registers the betrayal's cost — the purge of the member who chose the comfortable lie: Tank survives to strike Cypher down, and Trinity wakes to grief over Dozer's death, the body count landing on the survivors.
chain.caused_by_previous: Caused by ev-029's massacre: Cypher's murders and his being struck down by the surviving Tank produce the dead (Dozer, Apoc, Switch) and the wounded Tank that Trinity confronts on waking.

definition.name: The Hunter and the Hunted — the system's enforcement meets its exception
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Freedom vs. determinism — whether an ordered system can be broken by a choice it cannot compute.
definition.summary: Agent Smith opens by treating Neo as a manageable record to be wiped (ev-007) and closes by pronouncing Neo's death a 'settled inevitability' at the third-rail (ev-039), framing the whole pursuit as the system correcting an anomaly. Between those bookends the pursuit escalates and inverts: Smith is out-fought in the subway when Neo refuses the fate pronounced for him (ev-039), then entered and destroyed from within — the first Agent ever killed (ev-045) — leaving the surviving Agents to feel fear for the first time (ev-045). The chain establishes the plot's boldest claim about determinism: the enforcer of the script is undone by the one variable it could not predict, a human who chose to live (ev-039, ev-045).

chain.why_in_plot: This is the plot's opening bookend: Smith treats Neo as a record to be wiped, the system's enforcement in its purest form, and the summary anchors the whole pursuit here.
chain.caused_by_previous: First entry in the chain; Smith's decision to interrogate and erase 'Anderson' sets the enforcer-vs-anomaly conflict in motion.

chain.why_in_plot: The summary's pivot point: Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, out-fighting the enforcer at the third-rail — the variable the system cannot compute.
chain.caused_by_previous: The pursuit escalates from Smith's office assertion of control (ev-007) through the chase to the subway, where Smith again frames Neo's death as 'settled inevitability' and Neo rejects it.

chain.why_in_plot: The plot's closing bookend: Neo enters and destroys Smith — the first Agent ever killed — leaving the surviving Agents afraid, completing the inversion of enforcer and exception.
chain.caused_by_previous: Neo's refusal of the pronounced fate (ev-039) enables his resurrection and awakening, through which he reads the room as code and destroys Smith from within.
